decision: Deepen existing 6.2.2/lab 6-2/figure 6-2 and connect backward constraints in 11.2.3; no new structural item or adoption of paper speedups.
findings: OS row and column traffic depend on different matrix sizes. The largest-matrix-stationary rule and avoiding transpositions are heuristics, not a global search over all layers and parallelisms.
Partial AG/RdS operations require matching contraction indices; arbitrary local chunks can multiply unmatched indices. Blocking must respect hardware granularity and divisibility.
Analytical model separates launch, per-ring-step synchronization, bytes/bandwidth, prologue, steady state and epilogue; effective compute is calibrated and can be measured per local shape.

Most performance results simulate TPUv4-like 2D tori in SST/DRAMSim3, calibrated on four TPUv4 chips. FC simulated timings are combined with single-chip non-FC timings; they are not complete production-cluster measurements.

Table 3 distinguishes actual 4x4 TPUv4 FC utilization from estimated overlap. At the paper date, its JAX implementation cannot overlap AG/RdS with GeMM; compiler dependencies also restrict Wang overlap. No current TPU software-support claim follows.
1D baselines use only two ICI links whereas 2D uses four; this network-resource difference must not become a same-hardware algorithm-only speedup.
Communication model assumes independent directions/no ring contention. GPU logical meshes, memory-bound inference and MoE extensions are future work and require revised costs.
The statement that FSDP cannot strong-scale is not a general FSDP limitation and is not adopted. Do not infer training convergence or fixed-token-budget efficiency from weak-scaling FC utilization.

Table 3 real GPT-3 Collective 47.4% versus MeshSlice 45.5%, and Megatron 49.4% versus 47.1%, differ from projected-overlap values 65.7%/65.6%. These historical data are recorded only to distinguish measurement from projection, not as Qwen3 results.
